purpose: Ospemifene is used to treat moderate to severe painful intercourse (dyspareunia) and vaginal dryness in women who have gone through menopause. These symptoms happen because the vaginal tissues become thinner and drier after menopause when estrogen levels drop. This medication helps relieve that discomfort without being a traditional estrogen hormone.
how_it_works: Ospemifene works by acting like estrogen in certain parts of your body, especially in the vaginal tissues. It attaches to estrogen receptors in the vagina and helps keep the tissue healthier, thicker, and better moisturized. Think of it as a 'smart' estrogen-like pill that targets specific areas to help relieve your symptoms.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include hot flashes or hot flushes, vaginal discharge, muscle spasms, and increased sweating. Some women may notice some vaginal spotting or discharge. Most side effects are mild, but let your doctor know if anything bothers you.
warnings: This medication carries a boxed warning — the most serious type — because it may slightly increase the risk of stroke, blood clots, and uterine (endometrial) cancer, similar to estrogen products. Do not use it if you have had breast cancer, a history of blood clots, stroke, or heart disease. Tell your doctor about all your medical history and all medications you take before starting ospemifene.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 60 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day with food. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb it better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body.
